written_from: IBM z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385), the JOB statement's RESTART parameter (stepname, stepname.procstepname, *, checkid, the SYSCHK DD) and the EXEC statement's RD parameter, plus the COND / IF rules of slice 1. Written before any restart code ran on it. Second pass (2026-11-19) read the z/OS 3.1 JCL Reference (ieab600, JOB: RESTART 'Cautions when coding the RESTART parameter' and EXEC: COND 'When the JOB statement contains a RESTART parameter'): the COND and IF referback shapes that the first pass refused are answered there.
scenario_input: given: per step that starts in the restarted run, {rc: n}. Steps before the restart step have no entry (they do not execute).
scenario_answer: expect: per step, skipped (not executed because of the restart), run, or bypass (the COND / IF of the restart step or a later step kept it from starting).
flow_jcl: //* #8413 slice 4: JOB RESTART= (deferred step restart, procedure step,
//* RESTART=*, deferred checkpoint restart with SYSCHK, RD=). Answers in
//* scenarios.json, written from IBM's z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385
//* JOB RESTART) before any resolver ran.

scenarios.basis: RESTART=S3 without a checkid is a deferred step restart: the steps before S3 are not executed, S3 and every step after it are. S4's test (4,LT,S3) is false at rc 0.
The restart step and later steps keep their COND tests: S3 ends 8, so (4,LT,S3) is true and S4 is bypassed; S5's (0,NE) tests the steps executed so far (S3 only, A1), 8 NE 0 true, bypassed.
S5's bare COND=(0,NE) tests every preceding step that ran in this execution; the skipped steps have no return code this run (ASSUMED A1), so only S3 and S4 (both 0) are tested and S5 runs.
RESTART=* names the first step of the job: no step is skipped.
As a normal run: T3's (4,LT,T1) is true at rc 8.

RESTART=stepname.procstepname: stepname is the EXEC that calls the procedure, procstepname the procedure's step. Everything before CALL1.P2 (U0 and CALL1.P1) is skipped; P2, the rest of the procedure and the later job step run.
P3's COND=(4,LT,P2) names the restart step, which is allowed: rc 8 bypasses P3.

RESTART=(V3,CK1) with a SYSCHK DD before the first EXEC is a deferred checkpoint restart: V3 resumes at checkpoint CK1 (it still starts, and ends with a return code), the earlier steps are not executed, V4 runs.
RD=R on V3 governs automatic checkpoint restart after an abend of the running job; it does not change which steps a deferred restart runs.
The IF names the restart step W2, which ran in this execution: W2.RC = 0 is true, so the THEN clause (W3) runs.
W2.RC = 8 makes the IF false: the ELSE clause (W4) runs.

JOB RESTART, COND caution: a COND naming a step before the restart step has its return code test ignored (evaluated false); with every other test false the step runs. Z3's only test names Z1, so Z3 runs although Z2 ended 8.
EXEC COND, when the JOB has RESTART: a test naming the skipped M1 is false, but the other test (4,LT,M2) is evaluated normally; M2 ended 8, so it is true and M3 is bypassed.
As above with M2 at 0: both tests are false, so M3 runs.

EXEC COND, when the JOB has RESTART: the restart step becomes the first step of the job and the system evaluates any COND parameter on it as false and executes it. COND=ONLY on G2 would otherwise bypass it (no earlier step abended).
JOB RESTART, IF caution: a relational expression that references a step bypassed by RESTART is evaluated false. R1.RC = 0 is false, so the THEN step R3 is bypassed.
As above: E1.RC = 0 is false because E1 was bypassed by RESTART, so the ELSE clause (E4) runs.
JOB RESTART Example 3: RESTART=(*,CKPT2) restarts at checkpoint CKPT2 in the first job step; the SYSCHK DD follows the JOB statement. K1 still starts, no step is skipped.

JOB RESTART Example 4: RESTART=(PAY.WEEKLY,CHECK8): PAY is the EXEC that calls the procedure, WEEKLY the procedure step holding checkpoint CHECK8. The steps before WEEKLY are skipped, WEEKLY and AFTER run.

JCL Reference, EXEC: COND, 'COND parameter on an EXEC statement that calls a procedure' and 'When the JOB statement contains a RESTART parameter': the restart step is the first step to execute and its COND is ignored, so the override COND.K2=(0,LE) (which would bypass any step that follows a return code) does not stop K2. K3's own COND=(4,LT,K2) is not overridden and K2 ended 0, so K3 runs.

JCL Reference, EXEC: COND, 'COND parameter on an EXEC statement that calls a procedure' and 'When the JOB statement contains a RESTART parameter': a COND.procstepname override changes only the named step; K3 keeps COND=(4,LT,K2), which names the restart step, and K2 ended 8, so K3 is bypassed. AFTER has no COND and runs.

JCL Reference, EXEC: COND, 'COND parameter on an EXEC statement that calls a procedure' and 'When the JOB statement contains a RESTART parameter': COND.K3=(4,LT,CALL4.K2) replaces K3's COND=(8,LE,K1) and names the restart step, which executed: rc 8 is above 4, so K3 is bypassed.

JCL Reference, EXEC: COND, 'COND parameter on an EXEC statement that calls a procedure' and 'When the JOB statement contains a RESTART parameter': the same override with K2 ending 4: (4,LT,CALL4.K2) is false (4 is not less than 4), so K3 runs.

JCL Reference, EXEC: COND, 'COND parameter on an EXEC statement that calls a procedure' and 'When the JOB statement contains a RESTART parameter': COND.K3=(0,NE,U0) replaces K3's COND=(4,LT,K2), so K2's rc 8 no longer matters; the replacement names U0, a step before the restart step, and a COND test naming a step that did not execute in the restarted run is ignored (false), so K3 runs.

JCL Reference, EXEC: COND, 'COND parameter on an EXEC statement that calls a procedure' and 'When the JOB statement contains a RESTART parameter': an unqualified COND=(0,NE,U0) on the EXEC that calls the procedure applies to every procedure step and replaces K3's own COND=(4,LT,K2). The restart step K2 ignores its COND; K3's names the skipped U0 and is false, so K3 runs although K2 ended 8.

JCLLIB ORDER=(LIB.A,LIB.B): the system searches the libraries in the order given and uses the first that holds the member, so RPRC is LIB.A's (M1, M2, M3), not LIB.B's. RESTART=CALL1.M2 (stepname.procstepname) is a deferred step restart: U1 and M1 are before it and are not executed; M2 (its COND false) and every later step execute. M3's test (4,LT,M2) and U2's (4,LT,CALL1.M2) are false at rc 0.

Same restart as above with M2 ending rc 8: (4,LT,M2) is true (4 is less than 8), so M3 is bypassed, and U2's (4,LT,CALL1.M2) is true, so U2 is bypassed. A library procedure's steps are read exactly as an in-stream one's.
JCLLIB ORDER=(LIB.B,LIB.A): the first library holding RPRC is now LIB.B, whose member has steps N1 and N2; RESTART=CALL1.N2 is a step of that expansion (it would not be a step of LIB.A's RPRC).
RESTART=* restarts at the first job step; the first step here is the call CALL1, whose first executed step is the library member's M1, so nothing is skipped.

ONLYA is held only by LIB.A and ONLYB only by LIB.B: a member absent from the first library is taken from the next one in ORDER. RESTART=CALL2.B2 skips everything before it, including the whole first call.

assumed.text: A step skipped by the restart has no return code in the restarted run, so a bare COND=(code,op) (no stepname) reads only the steps that executed in it. IBM states the rule for a COND or IF that NAMES a skipped step (ignored / false), not for the bare form.

not_modelled: Automatic restart after a failure of the running job (RD=R / RNC, system restart): an action during a run, not a resubmission; the resolver reads JOB RESTART= only and does not read RD.

refused.construct: RESTART=(step,checkid) with no SYSCHK DD before the first EXEC
refused.reason: IBM: a checkid needs a SYSCHK DD placed immediately before the first EXEC; without it the JCL is in error

refused.construct: RESTART= naming a step the job does not have
refused.reason: IBM: the system cannot restart at a step that is not in the job

refused.construct: RESTART= naming the calling step of a procedure without a procstepname
refused.reason: IBM's syntax restarts at stepname.procstepname; the bare calling step is not stated

refused.construct: RESTART= naming a step name that appears twice in the job
refused.reason: IBM: the stepname and procstepname that identify the restart step must be unique within the job; otherwise the system cannot determine the restart step and results are unpredictable

library_jcl: //* #8413 restart, library procedures: the procedure is a member of a
//* JCLLIB library, not in-stream (JCL Reference, JCLLIB ORDER).

library_refused.construct: RESTART= naming the calling step of a library procedure without a procstepname
library_refused.reason: IBM: a restart inside a procedure is stepname.procstepname; the bare calling step is not a restart step

library_refused.construct: RESTART=CALL1.N2 when the member found first (LIB.A) has no step N2
library_refused.reason: IBM: the system cannot restart at a step that is not in the job; the member is the first one in ORDER

library_refused.construct: EXEC of a procedure that is in no JCLLIB library
library_refused.reason: IBM: the procedure cannot be found, the JCL is in error
